messages.subject_clean: dropping the 3838 port from url
messages.body_plain:
Well, the app needs a port to listen on, so you might change that port, but you cannot get rid of it. If you don't want to show the port to the world, and run the app as myserver.com <http://myserver.com> or myserver.com/myapp <http://myserver.com/myapp>, you need to redirect the webserver. When I set up my server, there was a part on this in the configuration tutorial, but I think it was in the rstudio-server documentation,

Anyway, what I did was putting

ProxyPass        /whiskyTastings/ http://localhost:3838/whiskyTastings/
ProxyPassReverse /whiskyTastings/ http://localhost:3838/whiskyTastings/
RedirectMatch permanent ^/whiskyTastings/$ /whiskyTastings/

into the virtual host part of the apache configuration.

messages.subject: Re: html output (e.g. from plotGoogleMaps) in shiny tabset
messages.subject_clean: html output (e.g. from plotGoogleMaps) in shiny tabset
messages.body_plain:
The problem is that plotGoogleMaps emits a full HTML file, which needs to be included as an IFrame in the Shiny App. Here is a minimal example. I have taken the basic example from the package vignette. You will notice that I use tags$iframe(srcdoc = ....) as the return value. What this does is returns the HTML file as a string, which is then embedded inline as an iframe. You can also include the myMap1.html file directly using tags$iframe(src = ...), but I am a little unclear as to its path in a Shiny app.

I have put this in a gist https://gist.github.com/ramnathv/275fe2a088e539f6b1ca so that you can copy and paste.

library(plotGoogleMaps)
library(shiny)
runApp(list(
  ui = pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel('Map'),
    sidebarPanel(""),
    mainPanel(uiOutput('mymap'))
  ),
  server = function(input, output){
    output$mymap <- renderUI({
      data(meuse)
      coordinates(meuse) = ~x+y
      proj4string(meuse) <- CRS("+init=epsg:28992")
      m <- plotGoogleMaps(meuse, filename = 'myMap1.html', openMap = F)
      tags$iframe(
        srcdoc = paste(readLines('myMap1.html'), collapse = '\n'),
        width = "100%",
        height = "600px"
      )
    })
  }
))

messages.body_plain:
Elodie,

Thanks for upgrading to the latest version, and for the information. It would be easier to help you with any issue you may run into now that you are using the latest version.

Now that you have posted your issue again, it is more clear that your issue is most likely a conflict of ports; you are using port 80 for Apache on the same server, right? Then, to best of my knowledge, you won't be able to use if for Shiny Server. Can you reconfigure your Apache to use a different port?

Besides that, I noticed a little problem in your configuration files that will cause a problem for you if you restart your Shiny Server.

- Please change your shiny-server.conf as follows: (note the line I have added to define log_dir)

> # Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
> run_as shiny;
>
> # Define a server that listens on port 3838
> server {
>   listen 80;
>
>   # Define a location at the base URL
>   location / {
>
>     # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
>     site_dir /srv/shiny-server;
>
>     # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
>     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>
>     # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
>     # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
>     directory_index on;
>   }
>   location /NHU133app {
>     app_dir /srv/shiny-server/NHU133app;

              log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>   }
> }

- Save the file
- Restart Shiny Server  (sudo restart shiny-server)

Best,
Fereshteh

  I have little knowledge about the mechanism of shiny, but found a way to solve such problem, though not convenient. Please take a look of my gist:

Best!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
messages.subject_clean: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
messages.body_plain:
Some information on this. I took choroplethr for a test drive on the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> site to see if that worked. The toy example that comes with the package works. http://patilv.shinyapps.io/choroplethrtestdrive/
I had to make an explicit call in server.r for the maps package. Even though it worked without that call locally, it popped an error on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. With the library(maps) call, the deployment was fine.

ui.r
------------
library(shiny)
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  plotOutput("pleth")
  ))

server.r
----------
library(shiny)
library(choroplethr)
library(maps)

data(county.fips, package="maps")
df = data.frame(region=county.fips$fips, value=sample(100, nrow(county.fips), replace=TRUE))
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$pleth=renderPlot({pleth=choroplethr(df, "county", 2)
                                 print(pleth)})

})
--------------------------------

messages.body_plain:
Vivek and Are,

Thank you so much for your help.  I will report all of this back to my user.

The requirement for library(maps) is interesting.  I am in the process of submitting my package to CRAN, and one of the things they came back with is that in my DESCRIPTION file some packages were miscategorized as "imports", "depends", etc.  These are the types of bugs which are undetectable to me when I develop, but seem to arise when my package interacts with other packages - basically, I think that the "library(maps)" requirement is indicative of a bug that I hope gets sorted out in the CRAN submission process.

Ari

messages.subject_clean: Add 'calculation in process' busy indicator for application need long time.
messages.body_plain:
It may be surprising but (if I understand you correctly) it's intended behavior. Switching tabs does just show and hide the tab's content, BUT, tabs that are not shown don't have their contents generated until they are shown. In other words, if a tab's output is invalidated while the tab is not shown, then that output will not be recalculated, not until the tab is shown. But once the tab is shown, then switching away from and back to that tab shouldn't cause any recalculation (unless, again, the output becomes invaliated in the meantime).

If you don't like this behavior, you can opt out of it on a per-output basis using the outputOptions function's suspendWhenHidden argument.

messages.subject: Continuous graph updating (as opposed to reload every time)
messages.subject_clean: Continuous graph updating (as opposed to reload every time)
messages.body_plain:
I've built a Shiny app to play a map based on different checkbox selections by the user.Depending on the checkbox, a different density is plotted on the map and it is reloaded. When the user changes the inputs the graph goes dim, waits a couple of seconds, and then reloads the new version which has lighter or darker colors on the states depending on the data.

My problem with this is that it doesn't create a smooth user experience with the graph. Ideally you'd see a map in front of you and when you change the input, have the states simply update their colors without having to reload the entire map.

Does anyone have experience with this or know a better way to do it? Here is an example of how I'm getting my map (based on a dataset I've dummied as 'percentages'):

states <- map_data("state")
states$percentage <- percentages$a
print(head(states))
map <- ggplot(states, aes(x=long, y=lat)) +
geom_polygon(aes(group=group, fill=percentage), col=NA,lwd=0) +
borders('state', colour = "grey")
map + scale_fill_gradient(low='white', high='red', limits = c(0,1))

Thanks.

messages.body_plain:
p.s. I did also find someone with a similar issue who talks about rebuilding packages as a possible fix?
http://apple.stackexchange.com/questions/120108/r-shiny-crash-on-loading-examples-cxa-guard-acquire-detected-deadlock-change

On Sunday, 9 February 2014 22:28:39 UTC+1, Mark Edmondson wrote:
> Hello, I sadly have this crash when trying to run the examples of Shiny on Mac OSX.  I have it running fine on Debian, but this is the first time I've tried on Mac.
>
> Following the guide found at https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md I have reinstalled R, RStudio and have re-downloaded the packages involved.
>
> However, when I try:
>
> R> library(shiny)
> R> runApp()
>
> ..Rstudio crashes saying "R Session Aborted" R encountered a fatal error
>
> Trying
>
> R> library(shiny)
> R> runExample("01_hello")
>
> ...I get the same.
>
> When I run the above in R standard, I get the below message dump, which I hope helps.
>
> I can only add that I had some trouble when attempting to install packages before reinstalling R and RStudio, I got an error saying RStudio couldn't delete the old packages.  I chmod the folder to 755, and deleted the package folders myself in the folder specified, then downloaded the latest version of RStudio - perhaps this is related?  I did:
>
> > sudo chown 755 /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/
>
> Permissions issue? If so what can I try?
>
> Yours sincerely,
> Mark

#(https://gist.github.com/xiaodaigh/7162506 <-- link to the password code)

tabPanel <- function(title, ..., value = NULL, condition = NULL) {
 divTag <- div(class="tab-pane",
 title=title,  `data-value`=value,`data-display-if` = condition,
     ...)
}

shinyUI(navbarPage("Report", id="report",  inverse = TRUE,

  tabPanel("Password",
    code,
    passwordTextInput("passInput","Enter password")),

       tabPanel(title="untested",condition="input.passInput=='passWD'",
             print("abcd"   )
))

messages.subject: conditionalPanel() in mainPanel() is shown, despite condition not being met
messages.subject_clean: conditionalPanel() in mainPanel() is shown, despite condition not being met
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
i posted this as an issue first on github, but i think that was the wrong place as i am not sure this is really an issue or me misunderstanding how shiny works.

i am trying to put a conditionalPanel inside the mainPanel. Whe i do, it gets displayed on refresh, after which the condition is evaluated, and the panel disappears if the condition is not met. I would expect it to not be displayed at all.
Excluding null/missing/empty variables in the condition does not help; it seems the condition simply does not get evaluated until after it's displayed.
toy example, using the example shiny application:

server.r:
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
    hist(dist)
  })

})

ui.r:

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("New Application"),
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("obs",
                "Number of observations:",
                min = 1,
                max = 1000,
                value = 500)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot"),
     conditionalPanel(condition = "input.obs==10", wellPanel(h4('you should not see me')))
  )
))

you'll see the 'you should not see me' header when you refresh the page.

In this example it's rather trivial, but i have an application that does an includeHTML() call in this way where it wrongly displays that HTMLpage for a couple of seconds.

Am i wrong in trying to use conditionalPanels this way?

anne

messages.subject: Re: error: argument is not interpretable as logical - ShinyRGL
messages.subject_clean: error: argument is not interpretable as logical - ShinyRGL
messages.body_plain:
I think this is a bug in ShinyRGL. If memory serves, ShinyRGL will try to plot whatever you return as a WebGL scene. So if you don't do something like plot3d() within your renderWebGL() function, it's not going to handle that case properly. It should check to see if you returned NULL before trying to plot the scene.

Feel free to open an issue here: https://github.com/trestletech/shinyRGL/issues and I'll take a look at this (hopefully) shortly.

Best,
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Who touched my shiny-app? A feature to track user's behavior.
messages.subject_clean: Who touched my shiny-app? A feature to track user's behavior.
messages.body_plain:
Yes, I think.

You can add this code in your server.R, like:

logTime <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y_%m_%d_%H_%M_%S");
fileLog <- paste("log", logTime, ".txt", sep = "")
file.create(fileLog)

This will create an empty txt file which can be used to save user behavior. Then add this code to write user behavior to that file:
observe({
  x <- iconv(input$tracking, from = "UTF-8")
  i <- as.numeric(regexpr("|", x, fixed = TRUE))
  L <- substr(x, 1, (i-1))
  V <- substr(x, (i+1), nchar(x))
  L <- paste('"', as.character(Sys.time()), " ", L, '": ', sep = "")
  if(grepl(",", V)) {
    V <- paste('["', gsub(",", '", "', V), '"],', sep = "")
  } else {
    V <- paste('"', V, '",', sep = "")
  }
  write(paste(L, V, sep = ""), fileLog, append = TRUE)
})

messages.body_plain:
Vincent / Winston,

I've actually realized that this is really a characteristic of Shiny as opposed to R or the map object. When you render a table and update it, Shiny dims the old version, waits for the updated one, and then displays. Is there any way I can tweak some setting or HTML to allow it to simply display the old version and replace as soon as the new one is ready?

On Friday, February 7, 2014 11:08:42 AM UTC-7, Blake Arensdorf wrote:
> I've built a Shiny app to play a map based on different checkbox selections by the user.Depending on the checkbox, a different density is plotted on the map and it is reloaded. When the user changes the inputs the graph goes dim, waits a couple of seconds, and then reloads the new version which has lighter or darker colors on the states depending on the data.
>
> My problem with this is that it doesn't create a smooth user experience with the graph. Ideally you'd see a map in front of you and when you change the input, have the states simply update their colors without having to reload the entire map.
>
> Does anyone have experience with this or know a better way to do it? Here is an example of how I'm getting my map (based on a dataset I've dummied as 'percentages'):
>
>
> states <- map_data("state")
> states$percentage <- percentages$a
> print(head(states))
> map <- ggplot(states, aes(x=long, y=lat)) +
> geom_polygon(aes(group=group, fill=percentage), col=NA,lwd=0) +
> borders('state', colour = "grey")
> map + scale_fill_gradient(low='white', high='red', limits = c(0,1))
>
>
>
> Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: No output graphics
messages.subject_clean: No output graphics
messages.body_plain:
Here is the source of your problem (most probably).

In ui.R you write

selectInput("dataset", "Choose a location",
  choices = c("Berlin Tigel Airport", "London City Airport", "Paris Charles De Gaulle")
)

and in server.R you check

input$dataset == "Berlin"

There is no way for the server to know that when you choose "Berlin Tigel Airport", it needs to use "Berlin" on the server side.

You can fix this by modifying your selectInput. Read ? selectInput to know what happens when you use a named vector in selectInput.

selectInput("dataset", "Choose a location",
  choices = c(
    "Berlin Tigel Airport" = "berlin",
    "London City Airport" = "london",
    "Paris Charles De Gaulle" = "paris"
  )
)

Hope this helps.

Hi Yinchong,

It is very difficult to even guess what is going on without any errors in the logs, or any other hints. So I just have to give you some suggestions:

2- I strongly suggest that you install the latest version of Shiny Server. The link to binary and documentation are here:

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#upgrading-from-shiny-server-0.3.x
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#quick-start

++ See if that changes the behavior of your applications
++ Check the server log in /var/log/shiny-server.log
++ Check in /var/log/shiny-server directory for an application specific log file. When your application terminates due to an error, there should be some information in this log file.

5- Is there any way that we could get access to your server/application? (you can send me private email if this is possible)

messages.subject_clean: Complex programming
messages.body_plain:
Good evening gentlemen!

Has complex programming and try to explain what I want through a reproducible example .

file server.R

library ( shiny )

segment_ll < - function (x, b0 , b1, b2 , X0) {
  ( b0 + b1 * x ) * ( x < = X0 ) +
  ( X0 * b0 + (b1 -b2 ) + b2 * x ) * ( x > x0 )
}

# Define server logic required to generate the plot
shinyServer (function ( input, output ) {

            datasetinput < - reactive ( {

              seq = x (1.10 )
              y = x +1.1 * 2 +0.5 * x ^ 2

              data <- data.frame (x, y)

            } )

            output $ contents < - renderTable ( {

              datasetinput ()

            } )

            # Listing the variables

            selectvarsdep output $ <- renderUI ( {

              dad < - datasetinput ( )

              if ( is.null ( dad) )
                return ( NULL )

              selectInput ( ' inVarsdep '
                          ''
                          names ( dad) )

            } )

            selectvarsindep output $ <- renderUI ( {

              dad < - datasetinput ( )

              if ( is.null ( dad) )
                return ( NULL )

              selectInput ( ' inVarsindep '
                          ''
                          names ( dad) )

            } )

            # Deslisadores linear to linear - segmented function
            slidersegllb0 output $ <- renderUI ( {
              sliderInput ( " insllb0 " , "Parameter b0 " , $ input = segll_minb0 min , max = $ segll_maxb0 input , input value = $ segll_minb0 )
            } )
            slidersegllb1 output $ <- renderUI ( {
              sliderInput ( " insllb1 " , "Parameter b1 " , $ input = segll_minb1 min , max = $ segll_maxb1 input , input value = $ segll_minb1 )
            } )
            slidersegllb2 output $ <- renderUI ( {
              sliderInput ( " insllb2 " , "Parameter b2 " , $ input = segll_minb2 min , max = $ segll_maxb2 input , input value = $ segll_minb2 )
            } )
            slidersegllX0 output $ <- renderUI ( {
              sliderInput ( " insllX0 " , "Parameter X0 " , $ input = segll_minX0 min , max = $ segll_maxX0 input , input value = $ segll_minX0 )
            } )

            # Deslisadores for your model
            output $ mins < - renderUI ( {

             expression1 < - grep ( ' [ [ : alpha: ] ] ' ,
                                 Unlist ( strsplit ( $ input yourmodel ,
                                                 ' [ [ : punct : ] ] ' ) ) ,
                                 value = T)

             expression2 < - grep ( ' x ' ,
                                 expression1
                                 value = T)

             parameters < - setdiff ( expression1 ,
                                   expression2 )

             expression3 < - paste ( paste ( ' function ( x , ' ,
                                        paste ( parameters ,
                                              collapse = ' ' )
                                        ')' ,
                                        sep ='' ) ,
                                  input $ yourmodel ,
                                  sep ='' )

             numinMin < - paste ( ' inMin '
                               parameters ,
                               sep ='' )

             cat ( paste ( paste ( ' $ output '
                             numinMin ,
                             " < - renderUI ( { NumericInput ( 'min ' ,
                             parameters ,
                             " ',' Minimum for "
                             sep ='' ) ,
                       parameters ,
                       " ' "
                       rep ( 1 , length ( parameters) ) ,
                       ' ) } ) "
                       sep = '' )
                 sep = ' \ n' )
            } )

            # Plotting the observed data
            plotDados output $ <- renderPlot ( {

              dad < - datasetinput ( )

              var_dep < - input $ inVarsdep
              var_indep < - input $ inVarsindep

              plot ( dad [ [ var_indep ] ] ,
                   dad [ [ var_dep ] ] ,
                   XLAB = var_indep ,
                   ylab = var_dep )

              # Plotanto the model on the observed data

                if (input == $ models ' segll ' ) {

                  curve ( segment_ll ( x , insllb0 $ input , $ input insllb1 , insllb2 $ input , $ input insllX0 )
                        min ( dad [ [ var_indep ] ] )
                        max ( dad [ [ var_indep ] ] )
                        T add = ,
                        col = 'red' )

                Else { }

                  seumodelo < - eval ( parse ( text = expression3 ( ) ) )

                }

            } )
} )

file ui.R

library ( shiny )

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI ( pageWithSidebar (
                        headerPanel ( ' Find the kicks of your initial nonlinear model ' ) ,

                        sidebarPanel (

                                           wellPanel (
                                               p ( strong ( 'Select one of the functions below ' ) ) ,
                                               selectInput ( ' models ' ,
                                                           ''
                                                           c ( ' segll ' ' -linear segmented linear ' = ,
                                                             'Other' = 'other' ) ) ,

                                               # Show only when the model is another
                                               conditionalPanel (
                                                                condition = " input.modelos == 'other '"
                                                                textInput ( ' yourmodel '
                                                                          ''
                                                                          'a + b * x ' ) )
                                               )

                                     wellPanel (
                                               p ( strong ( 'Select the dependent variable ' ) ) ,
                                               UIOutput ( ' selectvarsdep ')) ,

                                     wellPanel (
                                               p ( strong ( 'Select the independent variable ' ) ) ,
                                               UIOutput ( ' selectvarsindep ')) ,

                                     wellPanel (
                                               p ( strong ( ' Enter the limits (minimum and maximum) of the parameters' ) ) ,

                                               conditionalPanel (
                                                                condition = " input.modelos == ' segll '"
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_minb0 '
                                                                             " Minimum to b0 '
                                                                             1)
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_maxb0 '
                                                                             ' Maximum to b0 '
                                                                             4)
                                                                UIOutput ( ' slidersegllb0 ' ) ,
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_minb1 '
                                                                             ' Minimum for b1 '
                                                                             0.1 ) ,
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_maxb1 '
                                                                             ' Maximum for b1 '
                                                                             0.8 )
                                                                UIOutput ( ' slidersegllb1 ' ) ,
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_minb2 '
                                                                             ' Minimum for b2 '
                                                                             10)
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_maxb2 '
                                                                             ' Maximum for b2 '
                                                                             20)
                                                                UIOutput ( ' slidersegllb2 ' ) ,
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_minX0 '
                                                                             ' Minimum for X0 '
                                                                             10)
                                                                NumericInput ( ' segll_maxX0 '
                                                                             ' Maximum for X0 '
                                                                             20)
                                                                UIOutput ( ' slidersegllX0 ')) ,

                                               conditionalPanel (
                                                                condition = " input.modelos == 'other '"
                                                                UIOutput ( ' days ' )
                                                                )
                                               )
                                     )

                        mainPanel (
                                  tabsetPanel (
                                              TabPanel ( 'Data' , tableOutput ( ' contents' ) ) ,
                                              TabPanel ( ' graph ' , plotOutput ( ' plotDados '
                                                                             width = '900px '
                                                                             height = '700px ' ) )
                                              ) )
                        ) )

I would like to create the same panels whatever the role of the person placing . I know it's kind of complex , so ask the experts if it is possible what I want to do.

See you soon!

ui.R

server.R looks like this.

library(shiny)

library(datasets)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

datasetInput <- reactive({

# Return the requested dataset

switch(input$dataset,

"foo" = rock,

"Pressure" = pressure,

"Cars" = cars)

})

# Generate a summary of the dataset

output$summary <- renderPrint({

dataset <- datasetInput()

summary(dataset)

})

# Show the first "n" observations

output$view <- renderTable({

head(datasetInput(), n = input$obs)

})

})

## ui.R
### London weather

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel("Europe temperature 2013"),
sidebarPanel(

selectInput("dataset", "Choose a location",
choices = c("Berlin Tigel Airport" = "berlin",
"London City Airport" = "london",
"Paris Charles De Gaulle" = "paris")

  ),

dateRangeInput("daterange", "Date Range",
  start = "2013-01-01",
  end = "2013-12-31",
  min = "2013-01-01",
  max = "2013-12-31"
 )
),
mainPanel(
plotOutput("theGraph")
)
))

## server.R

### Weather server.R

library(shiny)
library(weatherData)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(plyr)

### load weather data.
berlin <- read.csv("berlin.csv", header = T)
london <- read.csv("london.csv", header = T)
paris <- read.csv("paris.csv", header = T)

shinyServer(function(input, output){

# Return the requested dataset

datasetInput <- reactive({
switch(input$dataset,
"berlin" = berlin,
"london" = london,
"paris" = paris)
})
# Prepare data once and then pass around the program.

output$theGraph <- renderPlot({
 foo <- datasetInput()
 foo$shortdate <- strftime(foo$Time, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
 foo$shortdate <- as.Date(foo$shortdate, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
 foo <- foo[foo$shortdate %in%
              seq.Date(input$daterange[1],
                       input$daterange[2], by = 1), ]

graphdata <- ddply(foo, .(shortdate), summarize, mean_C = mean(TemperatureC))

if(input$dataset == "berlin"){
theGraph <- ggplot(graphdata, aes(shortdate, mean_C)) +
geom_line() +
scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%Y-%m-%d")) +
xlab("") +
ylab("Mean Temperature (C)") +
ggtitle("2013 Average Daily Temperature in Berlin")
}

if(input$dataset == "london"){

theGraph <- ggplot(graphdata, aes(shortdate, mean_C)) +
geom_line() +
scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%Y-%m-%d")) +
xlab("") +
ylab("Mean Temperature (C)") +

ggtitle("2013 Average Daily Temperature in London")
}
if(input$dataset == "paris"){

theGraph <- ggplot(graphdata, aes(shortdate, mean_C)) +
geom_line() +
scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%Y-%m-%d")) +
xlab("") +
ylab("Mean Temperature (C)") +

ggtitle("2013 Average Daily Temperature in Paris")
}

print(theGraph)
})
})

#################

I would very, very strongly recommend NOT using eval() on any code that the user types. A user could easily run any command just by typing in some text with a call to system().

Here's a way to access an input with a name. If the text input is ID, then you can use this:
  input[[input$ID]]

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
I figured this would be better in a Gist.

Thanks, ZJ. I've actually been following those tutorials but can't seem to get the data back into R correctly. Hopefully you guys can take a look at this function and see where I'm going wrong, but I've basically tried to start by building it as simple as possible and then once I get it working I'll spend time wrapping it up and making it usable by others and understandable from a code perspective.

messages.body_plain:
Hello, I wondered if anyone would be able to help me with my frustration in trying to creating some "cascading" menu options for my app.

I'd like to be able to change options on menu's based on what has been selected from previous menus, i.e.

User chooses option A from menu1, menu2 displays A1,A2,A3.
User chooses option B from menu1, menu2 displays B1,B2,B3
etc.

I'd eventually like to have 3 layers of menu, then use the options selected for further work.

I thought this would be simple given updateSelectInput() but  just can't get it working, and so I hope someone here could help with my frustrations :)

I have also tried with renderUI(), but then I don't see how I can select the input value from that to get the other menu's to update.

I've tried to create an example below, here is my code:

SERVER.R
==========

library(shiny)

## test dataframe
df <- data.frame(option1 = c("A","A","B","B","C","C"),
                 option2 = c("A1","A2","B3","B1","C2","C3"),
                 option3 = c(T,F,T,F,T,F),
                 option4 = c("a","b","c","d","e","f"))

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  ## would like to be able to change the rows displayed here eventually
  output$table1 <- renderTable({
    df
  })

  ## for insight into what the menu vars are holding
  output$bugs <- renderText({
    text <- paste("menu1:", input$menu1,
                "menu2:", input$menu2,
                "menu3:", input$menu3)
  })

  ## expected behaviour - to show A, B or C
  ## actual - blank
  observe({
    if (is.null(input$menu1))
      return

    choice1 <- as.character(unique(df$option1))
#    names(choice1) <- 1:length(choice1)

    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "menu1",
                      choices = choice1)
  })

  ## expected behaviour - to show A1,B2,C etc based on what menu1 has chosen
  ## actual - doesn't update choices from default
  observe({
    if (length(input$menu1) < 2 )
      return()

    x <- input$menu1

    choice2 <- df[df$option1 == x,
                  "option2"]
    names(choice2) <- 1:length(choice2)

    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "menu2",
                      choices = choice2)
  })

  ## expected behaviour - to update choices based on menu3
  ## actual - no change
  observe({
    if (is.null(input$menu1) ||
          is.null(input$menu2) ||
          is.null(input$menu3)) ## these don't work, the input$menu's take the default list values
      return

    choice3 <- df[df$option1 == input$menu1 & df$option2 == input$menu2,
                  "option3"]

    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "menu1",
                      choices = choice3)
  })

  ## use these?
#   outputOptions(output, "menu1", priority = 1)
#   outputOptions(output, "menu2", priority = 2)
#   outputOptions(output, "menu3", priority = 3)

})

UI.R
====

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("Menu Test"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    textOutput("bugs"), #showing the values of the menu options below
    selectInput("menu1",
                "Menu1",
                choices = list("default1") #default, I would like this value to update
    ),
    selectInput("menu2",
                "Menu2",
                choices = list("default2") #default, I would like this value to update
                ),
    selectInput("menu3",
                "Menu3",
                choices = list("default3") #default, I would like this value to update
                )

  ),

  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("table1")
  )
))

messages.subject: Two or more select inputs with mutual exclusion
messages.subject_clean: Two or more select inputs with mutual exclusion
messages.body_plain:
This app generates two select inputs with mutual exclusion :

 - whenever the user selects the same value as the one in the other selector, this switches the two values
 - moreover, a subset of a dataframe is created and rendered according to the two selected columns, in such a way that the subdataframe never has two identical columns

code: https://gist.github.com/stla/9033053

run from url: devtools::source_url("https://gist.github.com/stla/9033053/raw/9c3ad4ce296397b923c88b40c2d43e4fbea8e4be/ShinyColumnsSelector.R")

I'd like to know your thoughts about :

 1) Easier solution ?
 2) How to do it for an arbitrary number of select inputs ?
 3) How to do it more user friendly (for the programmer) ?

messages.body_plain:
PS here's my code:
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  Siter <- reactive({input$Siter})

  Map <- reactive({
    do.call(file.remove,list(list.files("C:/Users/Clancy/Dropbox/R/My R Projects/shinyNewMapping/shinyNewMapping/www/Site.htm")))
    loc <- geocode(Siter())

    source('makeTradeRing.R')
    tR <- NULL
    for (i in 1:5){
      tR <- rbind(tR,makeTradeRing(loc[1],loc[2],i,500))
    }

    coordinates(loc) <- ~lon+lat
    proj4string(loc) <- CRS('+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84')
    m <- plotGoogleMaps(
      loc,zoom=13,mapTypeId = 'ROADMAP',
      fitBounds=F, openMap = F,
      add = T)

    tR <- data.frame(tR,id=rep("",nrow(tR)))
    names(tR) <- c('lon','lat','ID')
    coordinates(tR) <- ~lon + lat
    proj4string(tR) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84")

    ic = iconlabels(rep('.',nrow(tR)),height=10,colPalette = 'black')
    y<-plotGoogleMaps(tR,zoom=13,iconMarker=ic,
                      layerName="TradeRings",
                      clickable=F,
                      fitBounds=F,
                      mapTypeId = 'ROADMAP',
                      colPalette = 'black',
                      previousMap = m,
                      openMap=F,
                      filename = 'C:/Users/Clancy/Dropbox/R/My R Projects/shinyNewMapping/shinyNewMapping/www/Site.htm')
  })
  output$mapPlot <- renderUI({
    Map()
    tags$iframe(src='Site.htm',
                style = 'width: 750px; height: 700px')
  })

})

messages.body_plain:
Yes! My code is based on this example. However, my problem goes beyond the "Chang" example and coming up just as I have related to you. However,  I managed develop a reproducible minimum code. Change the values ​​in the field, and see what happens with sliderPanel. Then change to "Other" and see the error message. Thanks again for your help!

library(shiny)
runApp(list(
            ui =  basicPage(
                               selectInput('modelos',
                                           '',
                                           c('Linear' = 'lin',
                                             'Other' = 'outro')),
                               # Mostrar somente quando o modelo for outro
                               conditionalPanel(
                                                condition = "input.modelos == 'outro'",
                                                textInput('yourmodel',
                                                          '',
                                                          'a + b*x + c*x^2')),
                               conditionalPanel(
                                                condition = "input.modelos == 'lin'",
                                                numericInput('lin_minb0',
                                                             'Minimum to b0',
                                                             1),
                                                numericInput('lin_maxb0',
                                                             'Maximum to b0',
                                                             4),
                                                uiOutput('sliderlinb0'),
                                                numericInput('lin_minb1',
                                                             'Minimum para b1',
                                                             0.1),
                                                numericInput('lin_maxb1',
                                                             'Maximum para b1',
                                                             0.8),
                                                uiOutput('sliderlinb1')),

                               conditionalPanel(
                                                condition = "input.modelos == 'outro'",

                                                uiOutput('inputMin'),
                                                uiOutput('inputMax'),
                                                uiOutput('dyn_output'))
                                                ),
            server = function(input, output) {

             # Deslisadores para a função linear
             output$sliderlinb0 <- renderUI({
              sliderInput("insllb0", "Parameter b0", min=input$lin_minb0, max=input$lin_maxb0, value=input$lin_minb0)
             })
             output$sliderlinb1 <- renderUI({
              sliderInput("insllb1", "Parameter b1", min=input$lin_minb1, max=input$lin_maxb1, value=input$lin_minb1)
             })

             # Obtendo os parâmetros

             parameters <- reactive({

              expression1 <- grep('[[:alpha:]]',
                                  unlist(strsplit(input$yourmodel,

                                                  '[[:punct:]]')),
                                  value=T)
              expression2 <- c(grep('[[:alpha:]]{2,}',
                                    expression1,
                                    value=T),
                               grep('x',
                                    expression1,
                                    value=T))
              setdiff(expression1,
                      expression2)
             })

             # Número de parâmetros

             nparameters <- reactive({
              length(parameters())
             })

             # Criando os outputs para valores mínimos

             output$inputMin <- renderUI({
              inputs1 <- lapply(1:nparameters(), function(i) {
                                input_nameMIN <- paste("Minimo_para", i, sep=" ")
                                start_valMIN <- isolate(input[[input_nameMIN]])
                                if(is.null(start_valMIN)){
                                 start_valMIN <- i
                                }

                                numericInput(input_nameMIN, label = input_nameMIN, value = start_valMIN)

                      })
              #Put the inputs into a taglist

              do.call(tagList, inputs1)
             })

             # Criando os outputs para valrores máximos
             output$inputMax <- renderUI({
              inputs2 <- lapply(1:nparameters(), function(i) {
                                input_nameMAX <- paste("Maximo_para", i, sep=" ")
                                start_valMAX <- isolate(input[[input_nameMAX]])
                                if(is.null(start_valMAX)){
                                 start_valMAX <- i
                                }

                                numericInput(input_nameMAX, label = input_nameMAX, value = start_valMAX)

                      })

              #Put the inputs into a taglist

              do.call(tagList, inputs2)
             })

             #Criando os deslisadores
             output$dyn_output <- renderUI({
              outputs <- lapply(1:nparameters(), function(i) {
                                output_name <- paste("Parâmetro",i, sep=" ")
                                sliderInput(output_name,
                                            label = output_name,
                                            min = input[[input_nameMIN]],
                                            max = input[[input_nameMAX]],
                                            value = input[[input_nameMIN]])

                      })

              # Convert the list to a tagList - necessary for it to show

              do.call(tagList, outputs)
             })
            }
            ))

messages.subject: Re: Help with... 'help'

messages.body_plain:
You can test the current development version on Github -- the function includeMathJax() is a wrapper of tags$script(src = "...mathjax-src..."). MathJax expressions will work with uiOutput()/renderUI(), but popovers are a very special case, because the content of a pop over is stored in a character string when the HTML document is loaded, then MathJax won't see it since it is not part of the DOM. Modals work because the content is stored in a hidden div (i.e. "display: hide"), and MathJax can recognize math expressions even when they are hidden. To Stéphane: I do not think it is easy to get popovers work with MathJax. You can certainly aggressively call MathJax.Hub.Typeset() in the page but that does not sound like a good idea: tags$script(HTML("setInterval(function() {MathJax.Hub.Typeset();}, 100);")) Or you can add an .on("click") event on the button to typeset MathJax expressions after, say, 100 milliseconds. messages.body_plain:
According to this:
http://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/44928/what-is-the-default-projection-in-leaflet

the default projection in Leaflet is EPSG:3857 aka Google Mercator aka Web Mercator aka WGS84 aka Pseudo Mercator.

My understanding is that a map projection can be thought of as the function that takes a latitude and longitude as input, and outputs an x,y coordinate. So Google Geocoding doesn't "use" a projection at all.

I seem to vaguely recall having to work around some RJSONIO precision issues; is it possible that the lat/long is correct in your R code, but incorrectly being truncated on its way to the browser? Can you try this by calling leaflet methods with hardcoded lat/long coordinates and seeing if they're correct? Or by passing two different set of coordinates that differ by a small but significant distance, and see if they end up being distinguishable on the map?

messages.body_plain:
Sorry I renamed the function from includeMathJax() to withMathJax() in the development version. For static content, you only need to call withMathJax() once, but for dynamic UI output, you have to call withMathJax() every time you render new math expressions in the page. Below is an example of popovers; note I used the option `data-html`=true to make sure withMathJax() can typeset the math expressions after the popover is rendered, and as the documentation of Twitter Bootstrap has indicated, this may have potential security problems: http://getbootstrap.com/2.3.2/javascript.html#popovers helpPopup <- function(title, content, placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'), trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual')) { tagList( tags$a( href = "#", class = "btn btn-mini", `data-toggle` = "popover", `data-html` = "true", title = title, `data-content` = content, `data-animation` = TRUE, `data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1], `data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1], tags$i(class="icon-question-sign") ), tags$script("$(\"a[data-toggle='popover']\").popover();") ) } runApp(list( ui = fluidPage( h1('Math demo'), withMathJax(helpText('static content $$\\sqrt{2}$$')), helpText('more static content $$1-\\frac{1}{2}$$'), uiOutput('foo') ), server = function(input, output, session) { output$foo = renderUI({ list(helpPopup("Test Math",withMathJax(HTML('math here $$\\alpha^2$$')))) }) } )) Regards, Yihui On Mon, Feb 17, 2014 at 3:05 PM, Yihui Xie wrote: > You can test the current development version on Github -- the function > includeMathJax() is a wrapper of tags$script(src = > "...mathjax-src..."). MathJax expressions will work with > uiOutput()/renderUI(), but popovers are a very special case, because > the content of a pop over is stored in a character string when the > HTML document is loaded, then MathJax won't see it since it is not > part of the DOM. Modals work because the content is stored in a hidden > div (i.e. "display: hide"), and MathJax can recognize math expressions > even when they are hidden. > > To Stéphane: I do not think it is easy to get popovers work with > MathJax. You can certainly aggressively call MathJax.Hub.Typeset() in > the page but that does not sound like a good idea: > > tags$script(HTML("setInterval(function() {MathJax.Hub.Typeset();}, 100);")) > > Or you can add an .on("click") event on the button to typeset MathJax > expressions after, say, 100 milliseconds. > > Regards, > Yihui > > > On Wed, Feb 12, 2014 at 7:29 PM, Vincent wrote: >> Ah. messages.subject: Best way to handle upload of large data files?
messages.subject_clean: Best way to handle upload of large data files?
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I'm currently switching an RGtk2 app over to shiny. The main part of the app is to facilitate an analysis pipeline. The datafiles that gets analysed are rather large (500 mb+) so uploading them is rather time-consuming, especially as they are already available to R if you are running the app locally.

The question is thus how to best handle this scenario? My wish list is:

Have a graphic file selecter as with <input type='file'/>
Avoid copying the file to a temporary location if already available (app running locally)
Fallback to uploading if the file is not available (app running on server)

Is this possible at all? For the sake of user-friendliness I would really like to avoid having users type in the file path manually in a text field...

best

Thomas

Now I am adding another function which enables users to input a precise column interval and zoom in that part of heatmap. He is satisfied with this selection and want to update the value to the current sliderInput. But now after updating, the sliderInput shows 205 instead of 200, which causes confusion.

output$v.xyz <- renderUI({
input$xyz
})
}

runApp(list(ui=ui,server=server))

Is there another way to achieve this ?

messages.subject: Plotting one graph on top of another
messages.subject_clean: Plotting one graph on top of another
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
 I am working on an app where the user will choose what  points to plot  on a map (raster). Right now I am using a single renderPlot()  to assemble the graph - first the raster is plotted and then the points are plotted on top of the raster. When the user makes different choices the whole thing is plotted again. The raster part takes much longer to plot than the points, so there is a considerable lag between choosing a new set of points and the graph re-drawing. Joe Cheng responded to a different question and showed how to make it so the graph does not gray out when it is recalculating. That is helpful, but I am wondering if there is some way to first send the raster as one renderPlot(), and then do the points in a second renderPlot and somehow combine the two on the UI side, and thus speed things up.

Thanks

John Paul

messages.subject_clean: shiny server on OSX
messages.body_plain:
The launcher.cc file needs to be edited to use the proc_pidpath() function on OSX instead of Linux proc. If you apply the changes outlined in Nathan Weeks' commit here <https://github.com/nathanweeks/shiny-server/commit/d5240ef6d795dafc89c74a49d6f14d7fe0509541#commitcomment-5425046> and then recompile (run through the cmake part of the install) then it will work fine one Macintosh OSX.

-Mark

>
> /proc/XXXXX/exe doesn't exist--got Linux?
>
> Any wisdom?
>
> Thanks,
> Dan
>

> >

messages.subject: Re: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.subject_clean: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.body_plain:
In the next version of shiny passing callback functions to DataTables will hopefully be allowed. It should be easier to implement then. For now... Every time renderDataTable() is re-executed a new DataTables object is created with a new id that you need to create a FixedHeader object for in addition to removing FixedHeader object of the previous DataTable. You need to catch the event of creating this new DataTable (try setting some onclick/onchange event handlers or MutationObserver to catch DOM changes), but you also need to catch the event of moving between tabs, when DataTable objects get hidden and FixedHeader objects must get hidden as well. So, it's not as easy as adding couple of lines of code to ui.R. I agree that it would be great to get it built-in in the next versions of shiny.

messages.subject: How about an indication if uploaded file is too large?
messages.subject_clean: How about an indication if uploaded file is too large?
messages.body_plain:
I just spent several hours trying to figure out why my app did not react when I uploaded a file. I eventually realized that the file exceeded the default max size. To quote from the relevant tutorial:

> By default, Shiny limits file uploads to 5MB per file. You can modify this limit by using the shiny.maxRequestSize option. For example, adding options(shiny.maxRequestSize=30*1024^2) to the top of server.R would increase the limit to 30MB.

Unfortunately the behavior seems to be to not react at all. For example, I had the following code:
> rawData.trigger <- reactive({
>             message( " ... rawData.trigger STARTING" )
>             inFile <- input$rawDataFile
                                 :
                                 :
          })
If the selected file exceeds the limit, my message never appears (i.e., the reactive function never gets invoked) so the problem is not readily identifiable, even though it is easily fixed. It would be a big help if Shiny could provide some sort of warning or error indication when this type of "user error" takes place. If this had been a deployed app being used by somebody else, they would be frustrated and I would be mystified.

messages.subject: Re: Improvement ideas
messages.subject_clean: Improvement ideas
messages.body_plain:
For 4), it is now possible in the development version:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny You can type a string of the form
"lower, upper" to specify a range to filter a column. For example,

runApp(list(
  ui = fluidPage(
    dataTableOutput('tab1')
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$tab1 = renderDataTable(iris)
  }
))

You can type "4,5" (without quotes) in the search box of the first
column so that the rows are filtered using  Sepal.Length >=4 &
Sepal.Length <=5.

"lower," means [lower, Inf], and ",upper" means [-Inf, upper].

For 5), I believe it is also possible with the current development
version; see an example at https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/356

Thanks for all the ideas and feedback!

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.subject_clean: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I just added experimental support for this in the development version:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/

You need to download the FixedHeader plugin from
http://datatables.net/extras/ and put dataTables.fixedHeader.js under
www/ (if you put it in other directories, you need to adjust the path
in tags$script() below accordingly). Then this should work:

# ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
    dataTableOutput('tab1'),
    tags$head(
      tags$style(type='text/css', '.fixedHeader table.table thead
.sorting { background-color: #eee; }'),
      tags$script(src='dataTables.fixedHeader.js')
    )
))

# server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    output$tab1 = renderDataTable(iris, callback='function(oTable) {
new FixedHeader(oTable); }')
})

Please test it if you can. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

I think that is a good idea and I just added a 'callback' argument in
renderDataTable() so that users can easily use the DataTable instance
to do whatever they want. An example is given in my previous reply.

On Fri, Feb 21, 2014 at 9:03 AM, Dmitri <dmitr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> In the next version of shiny passing callback functions to DataTables will
> hopefully be allowed. It should be easier to implement then. For now...
> Every time renderDataTable() is re-executed a new DataTables object is
> created with a new id that you need to create a FixedHeader object for in
> addition to removing FixedHeader object of the previous DataTable. You need
> to catch the event of creating this new DataTable (try setting some
> onclick/onchange event handlers or MutationObserver to catch DOM changes),
> but you also need to catch the event of moving between tabs, when DataTable
> objects get hidden and FixedHeader objects must get hidden as well. So, it's
> not as easy as adding couple of lines of code to ui.R. I agree that it would
> be great to get it built-in in the next versions of shiny.

messages.subject: Is it possible to toggle off Reactivity?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to toggle off Reactivity?
messages.body_plain:
Question:

Is it possible to temporarily turn off reactivity?  I have used Shiny to write a couple simulation programs where sometimes it would be nice to turn reactivity off, to be able to toggle a number of settings at once, and then turn it back on.  This would be especially helpful on a slider/number input where I allow users to increase the number of simulations run.  As it stands, Shiny is too smart for its own good.

For example, if by default Simulations = 100

If you type two zeros in a textbox, to run 10,000 simulations, Shiny automatically runs 1000 simulations before it runs 10,000.   Which is a tad confusing to the user.

To that end, is there a way to use Shiny to mimic a typical submit form approach?  I like Shiny because it's great to have R behind a web server, it works great and I'm highly productive in it, and in general reactivity is awesome.  But there are also times I'd like to use R without the reactivity.  In the past I've used Python + any of the web frameworks, but I like R.

Thanks!
Erik

messages.subject_clean: Downloading plots using downloadHandler()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jui-Hua Hsieh,

I've been having the same problem, but I've found a workaround.

Create a new function called select_plot2 that contains the same body as select_plot.

Instead of having it be reactive, structure it like this

select_plot2 = function() {

       ### INSERT CODE FROM select_plot

}

Then call select_plot2() from within your downloadHandler (instead of select_plot).

Like this:

output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() { paste(input$proftype, '.png', sep='') },
    content = function(file) {
      png(file)

      #select_plot()
      select_plot2()
      dev.off()
    }
  )

None of the advice/solutions posted on this thread have worked for me, but this did. I'm not sure what the bug is with the reactive construct, but this seems to work.

messages.subject_clean: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.body_plain:
Check this example:

# ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  selectInput('spec',"Species",levels(iris$Species)),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("Tab 1",dataTableOutput('tab1')),
    tabPanel("Tab 2", NULL)

  ),
  tags$head(
    tags$style(type='text/css', '.fixedHeader table.table thead .sorting { background-color: #eee; }'),

    tags$script(src='dataTables.fixedHeader.min.js'),
    tags$script(src='jquery-ui.min.js') # http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jqueryui/1.10.4/jquery-ui.min.js
  )
))

# server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$tab1 = renderDataTable(iris[iris$Species==input$spec,], callback='
function(oTable) {
  new FixedHeader(oTable);
  oTable.on("remove", function () {
    $("table:not([id])[aria-describedby^=\'"+oTable.attr("id")+"\']").parent().remove()
  })
}')
})

Endless amount of header objects is created every time you change input$spec, I added a fix for that. However, I can't come up with an elegant fix for header objects always staying visible when switching tabs.

I've a question about manipulation of datasets.

I'm trying to make a small program which can "remember" the last entries in a numericInput - field.

For example:

What I were able to do was just to overwrite the one field of the matrix with the numericInput. But my problem is, I want to change for example the field [1,2] to 2, the field [2,1] to 3 and [2,2] to 4. This matrix should than be plotted as output.
If I now change the first field again, the last Input must not be remembered anymore, I just want all four fields with the actual values in one matrix.

I don't want four different numericInputs, because this wouldn't work in my situation.

I'm just wondering if it's possible to safe the changed matrix after each step. And then iteratively take the new matrix for the next manipulation.

thanks for all kind of ideas and suggestions.

Kind Regards

Jürg

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to perform a system call to run an external program and pipe in the unbuffered stdout into my shiny app. I am attempting to do this via a named pipe. Basic steps: a named pipe is created, the external application is called with stdout directed to the pipe, then I use a while loop to consume each line in the pipe. The problem is that all of the lines in the pipe are rendered in the app after the loop exits, rather than line by line. I'm not sure how to restructure this in order to instruct shiny to update output$wnText with each pass through the loop.

I have the following in server.R:

    runWN <- reactive({
      if(length(input$run_wn) > 0 && input$run_wn == 1){ #check that user has requested a windninja run
         system("mkfifo wnpipe")
         system(paste("/home/natalie/windninja_trunk/build/src/cli/./WindNinja_cli",
                "windninja.cfg >> wnpipe",
                collapse=""), intern=FALSE, wait=FALSE)
         fileName="wnpipe"
         con=fifo(fileName,open="rt",blocking=TRUE)
         linn = " "
         #linn is not printed each time cat is called, just one long string after the while loop exits
         while ( length(linn) > 0) {
           linn=scan(con,nlines=1,what="character", sep=" ", quiet=TRUE)
           cat(linn,"\n"); flush.console()
         }
         close(con)
         unlink ("wnpipe")
       }
    })

    output$wnText <- renderPrint({
         runWN()
    })

I appreciate any suggestions.

Natalie

2) does anyone know where I might find information about installing X11 on Amazon EC2 linux instance? I did google <https://www.google.com/search?q=X11+on+Amazon+EC2+linux+instance&oq=X11+on+Amazon+EC2+linux+instance&aqs=chrome..69i57.309j0j7&sourceid=chrome&espv=210&es_sm=119&ie=UTF-8#q=install+X11+on+Amazon+EC2+linux+instance> it, but it's a lexicon I'm not entirely familiar with (and, maybe there's a simple fix someone knows about).

I realize this may also be related to shiny-server.

Thanks!
Dan

PS I am very grateful for the work you all do on development projects like this and ggplot2 and dplyr, etc. These sorts of tools are genuinely changing the way I think and do business.

Check this example:

# ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  selectInput('spec',"Species",levels(iris$Species)),

  tabsetPanel(

    tabPanel("Tab 1",dataTableOutput('tab1')),

    tabPanel("Tab 2", NULL)

  ),

  tags$head(

    tags$style(type='text/css', '.fixedHeader table.table thead .sorting { background-color: #eee; }'),

    tags$script(src='dataTables.fixedHeader.min.js'),

    tags$script(src='jquery-ui.min.js') # http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jqueryui/1.10.4/jquery-ui.min.js

  )

))

# server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$tab1 = renderDataTable(iris[iris$Species==input$spec,], callback='

function(oTable) {

  new FixedHeader(oTable);

  oTable.on("remove", function () {

    $("table:not([id])[aria-describedby^=\'"+oTable.attr("id")+"\']").parent().remove()

  })

}')

})

It still might be useful to have some custom event triggered when switching tabs, as I'm not aware of any easy way to capture this event (apart from using mutations, which I don't consider proper either). It should be easy to add and will solve many potential problems like the one I described above. BTW, what's the "official" way to assign a callback function now: options = list(fnInitComplete=I('function here')) or callback = 'function here' (I mean the approach that will go to the next release)? I personally like the first approach more, as it's much more flexible and allows to use other callbacks. E.g. to add conditional formatting that has to be re-applied after every sorting needs fnDrawCallback.

Hello,

I've added a leaflet map to my website based on the mapbox example provided online. I'm trying to use the latitude/longitude output from mapclick as a variable to input a file I have on the server. In other words, I would like the user to be able to click on the map and in the background a certain file (with a lat/lon name) is called. I'm not sure how to do this so that the variable is recognized.

In my server.r I have something like:

wd is the working directory

filelist <- list.files(wd)
x <- as.numeric(substring(filelist,6,12))
y <- as.numeric(substring(filelist,14,21))
lata <- substring(filelist[which.min(abs(x-input$map_click$lat))],6,12) #
lona <- substring(filelist[which.min(abs(y-input$map_click$lng))],14,21)
FILES <- filelist[intersect(which(substring(filelist,6,12) == lata),which(substring(filelist,14,21) == lona))]

FILES produces text with the filename I am trying to access (i.e. data_41.0625_-73.5625).

So based on input$map_click$lat & input$map_click$lng (where the user clicks on the map) I am able to find the nearest lat/lon file where I have data. I want to be able to reactively access FILES based on the map click so that it can be read in as data.

I hope this is clear and thanks in advance for any input you have.

-Sarah

messages.subject: Re: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.subject_clean: Fixed Header Shiny DataTables
messages.body_plain:
The new 'callback' argument in renderDataTable() is not the same thing
as DataTables callback functions. Instead, it is only a function with
one argument 'oTable' that is the DataTable instance created for the
table. You can manipulate this instance using the 'callback' function.
This is what it basically does:

oTable = $('#foo').dataTable({ options })
callback(oTable)

It is irrelevant to DataTables callbacks such as fnInitComplete
(http://datatables.net/usage/callbacks), which are part of the
initialization options and must be passed in using the 'options'
argument in renderDataTable().

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to toggle off Reactivity?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to toggle off Reactivity?
messages.body_plain:
I use HTML UI for a lot of things, so perhaps this solution would work for a submit button type case.

* Use hidden values for the reactive variables
* Use standard inputs for what we want to change
* Bind a JS function to a submit button that, when clicked, changes the hidden input value.
* Reactive listened will pick up that change and update everything appropriately.

Which is a little different from a toggle for reactivity on and off.  Patrick's solution would work to (use number field, limit to 0 and 1, or just query UI and make a on/off toggle)

I do think it would be a nice to be able to have a on/off reactivity slider built in the standard UI as I imagine wanting to turn off the reactivity would be a common scenario (and also a way to reduce server load).

Erik

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to store and utilize client data
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to store and utilize client data
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This is a great question and one we aimed to tackle in Shiny Server Pro. ShinyApps will also expose the ability to ask users to login before granting them access to the app. You can use things like LDAP and Active Directory if you're deploying inside an organization, but you may be more interested in the soon-to-be-released Google auth feature. This feature will allow users to login using their Google account which is exposed to your Shiny application.

This allows you to store settings or data unique to the current user in a Shiny process. We'll be working to put together more examples of this functionality over the coming weeks and will certainly have something ready by the time we launch the feature on ShinyApps.io.

FYI Andrew, ShinyApps will eventually be replacing Glimmer and Spark. We're not in a rush, but the stability, scalability, and reliability of ShinyApps will be much greater. We'll also be rolling out new features like authentication uniquely on ShinyApps moving forward. So take it for a spin when you have a chance and let us know what you think!

Best,
Jeff

Stephane - instead of including the UTF-8 character directly, you can also specify Unicode values in strings with something like "\U2264". The string "\U2264 \U221E" is equivalent to "≤ ∞", and it can be read more reliably across platforms.

The result is the same (again, on my Mac):
> "\U2264 \U221E"
[1] "≤ ∞"
> "≤ ∞"
[1] "≤ ∞"

Does this app work for you in Windows?

runApp(list(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    numericInput('n', 'N', 100),
    verbatimTextOutput('textout')
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$textout <- renderText({ paste(input$n, "\U2264 \U221E") })
  }
))

-Winston

messages.subject: Two issues with iframes using navbarPage
messages.subject_clean: Two issues with iframes using navbarPage
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am making an app using the navbarPage layout (shiny devel version 0.8.0.99). The app is very simple, just a social media/content aggregator, where the navbar menus represent my website, blog, previous shiny apps I've made, etc. I use iframes to embed the content in the app. However, there are two issues. And perhaps I would have the same issues in another shiny version, and even if not using navbarPage. I don't think it necessarily has to do with navbarPage; that just happens to be what I am using.

1. The iframes I use to embed shiny apps appear to load the initial ui.R in the browser, but no plots will appear and the app is not responsive when I click on fields in the iframe. I can "click" things, but there is no reactivity. If I am very quick to click on a navbar menu to display an iframe-embedded shiny app as soon as this app loads, then the app inside the iframe will run, plots will plot, it's responsive, and reactivity is present. The iframe-embedded app inside this app runs fine. But for some reason if I just let my app load for a second, and then casually visit the page via the navbar where another app is shown in an iframe, somehow it's "too late" and any embedded apps do not work.

2. The second issue is somewhat ironic in comparison to the first. If I can find a way to make my apps in iframes responsive and reactive, I then also have to find away to get them to NOT all load inside their iframes when I first launch my app. There are way too many! (Many more than shown below.) I would like to prevent the content from loading while it is hidden at app launch, and only load the content in an iframe once it is made visible by clicking on the appropriate navbar menu option. The only ways I know of to do things like this are with action buttons and isolate(). Is there some kind of way I can combine isolate() perhaps with tabPanel IDs to prevent loading lots of hidden iframes when I load the app?

Here is some example navbarPage code that I experience these two issues with:

navbarPage("Matt Leonawicz",
tabPanel("Website", fluidRow( column(12, "", mainPanel(tags$iframe(src="http://statmatt.com/", width="1150", height="925"))) ), id="website"),
tabPanel("Blog", fluidRow( column(12, "", mainPanel(tags$iframe(src="http://blog.snap.uaf.edu/", width="1150", height="925"))) ), id="snapblog"),
navbarMenu("Other Apps",
tabPanel("Sea ice & winds", fluidRow( column(12, "", mainPanel(tags$iframe(src="http://shiny.snap.uaf.edu/sea_ice_winds/", width="1150", height="925"))) ), id="app_ice_winds"),
tabPanel("Sea ice coverage", fluidRow( column(12, "", mainPanel(tags$iframe(src="http://shiny.snap.uaf.edu/sea_ice_coverage/", width="1150", height="925"))) ), id="app_ice_cov"),
tabPanel("Temperature & winds", fluidRow( column(12, "", mainPanel(tags$iframe(src="http://shiny.snap.uaf.edu/temp_wind_events/", width="1150", height="925"))) ), id="app_temp_wind")
)
)

Thanks,
Matt
